question: An old post links https://stellarlight.xyz/project/passport. What is that project now, and is it still active?

golden.answer: Use `scout.resolveProject` with the old slug or URL and cite the response's `meta.generatedAt` as the as-of date (observed value `2026-11-02T16:34:40.509Z`). As observed on 2026-11-02, the query `passport` matched on slug. The matched record is `Stellar Passport` (slug `passport`) with status Draft, and `superseded` is true. The `current` record is slug `stellar-passport`, name `Stellar Passport`, status Live, at https://stellarlight.xyz/project/stellar-passport. The response's `evidence` block describes the matched record, not the current one: `statusAsOf` 2026-08-17, basis `site-liveness`, source https://demo.stellarpassport.xyz/, and `unsourced` false. Resolving `stellar-passport` directly returns the current record's evidence: `statusAsOf` 2026-09-06, basis `human-verified`, source https://stellarpassport.xyz/. Both records carry the same name, so the old slug is a superseded duplicate directory record, not a real-world rename; the project site https://stellarpassport.xyz/ is live under the same name. Site-liveness means only that a page answered, so do not present it as proof of product activity. Scout lists Stellar Passport as an SCF-funded passkey-secured onboarding and identity platform.
